labeller: The AI coding agent that implemented this study (Claude), working from the static review page (the maps and tables in kitchener-geo04-review.html) and the candidate metrics. No field visit, no imagery, no OSM history consulted while labelling correspondence.

definition_changes.when: after the six virtual links, before any unofficial connection was labelled
definition_changes.change: obvious_correspondence now covers, for an unofficial connection as for a virtual link, the same connection along or across the same road; the not_comparable example 'an on-road route with no facility of its own' was removed.

definition_changes.when: after 20 records, before the remaining curb-cut records
definition_changes.change: A label may cite a tagged OSM node near the record as well as a candidate way, so a facility OSM carries only as a node (a kerb at a corner) is recorded as such. Earlier labels were re-checked: 393902 and 388243 cite the crossing their stub leads onto; 393902's topology was revised to topology_disagreement for the crossing OSM lacks.

records.note: No OSM crossing of Wexford Crescent here: footway C3 ends at the south sidewalk (C2); the City's link carries it across to the north sidewalk (C4).

The City splits the Wilhelm Street sidewalk at a railway crossing with an 8.7 m virtual link; OSM carries it inside sidewalk C1 (with sidewalks 11922 and 11924) and marks the rails with a railway=crossing node.

A 3 m virtual link where the Ottawa Street South sidewalk crosses rails; OSM carries it inside a 338 m sidewalk way with a railway=crossing node.
